Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (26 April 121 – 17 March 180) was Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher, belonging to the Nerva–Antonine dynasty—the last of the Five Good Emperors and the final emperor of the Pax Romana. Born to Marcus Annius Verus and Domitia Calvilla, he was raised by his mother and paternal grandfather after his father’s death and adopted by Antoninus Pius, who became emperor after Hadrian’s death. Marcus studied under tutors like Herodes Atticus and Marcus Cornelius Fronto and married Antoninus’s daughter Faustina in 145. After Antoninus died in 161, he ruled alongside his adoptive brother Lucius Aurelius Verus amid military conflicts, including the Parthian War of Lucius Verus and the Marcomannic Wars, while addressing challenges from Germanic peoples and reducing silver purity in the currency. The Antonine Plague, which erupted in 165 or 166, caused significant population loss, and Lucius Verus may have died from it. Following his death in 180, his son Commodus succeeded him—a topic of historical debate. His legacy includes the celebrated *Meditations*, a key text in Stoic philosophy, and enduring monuments in Rome commemorating his military achievements.

<mark>**Marcus Aurelius Antoninus**</mark><mark> (</mark>[<mark>/ɔːˈriːliəs/</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English)<mark> </mark>[<mark>*or-EE-lee-əs*</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key)<mark>;[2] Latin: </mark>[<mark>[ˈmaːrkʊs au̯ˈreːli.us antoːˈniːnʊs]</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Latin)<mark>; 26 April 121 – 17 March 180) was </mark>[<mark>Roman emperor</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_emperor)<mark> from 161 to 180 and a </mark>[<mark>Stoic</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoicism)<mark> philosopher. He was a member of the </mark>[<mark>Nerva–Antonine dynasty</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerva%E2%80%93Antonine_dynasty)<mark>, the last of the rulers later known as the </mark>[<mark>Five Good Emperors</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Good_Emperors)<mark> and the last emperor of the </mark>[<mark>Pax Romana</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pax_Romana)<mark>, an age of relative peace, calm, and stability for the </mark>[<mark>Roman Empire</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire)<mark> lasting from 27 BC to 180 AD. He served as </mark>[<mark>Roman consul</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_consul)<mark> in 140, 145, and 161.</mark>
<mark>Marcus Aurelius was the son of the </mark>[<mark>praetor</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praetor)<mark> </mark>[<mark>Marcus Annius Verus</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Annius_Verus_(father_of_Marcus_Aurelius))<mark> and his wife </mark>[<mark>Domitia Calvilla</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domitia_Calvilla)<mark>. He was related through marriage to the emperors </mark>[<mark>Trajan</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trajan)<mark> and </mark>[<mark>Hadrian</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadrian)<mark>. Marcus was three when his father died, and he was raised by his mother and </mark>[<mark><u>paternal grandfather</u></mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Annius_Verus_(II))<mark>. After Hadrian's </mark>[<mark>adoptive</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption_in_ancient_Rome)<mark> son, </mark>[<mark><u>Aelius Caesar</u></mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aelius_Caesar)<mark>, died in 138, Hadrian adopted Marcus's uncle </mark>[<mark>Antoninus Pius</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoninus_Pius)<mark> as his new heir. In turn, Antoninus adopted Marcus and </mark>[<mark>Lucius</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucius_Verus)<mark>, the son of Aelius. Hadrian died that year, and Antoninus became emperor. Now heir to the throne, Marcus studied Greek and Latin under tutors such as </mark>[<mark>Herodes Atticus</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herodes_Atticus)<mark> and </mark>[<mark>Marcus Cornelius Fronto</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Cornelius_Fronto)<mark>. He married Antoninus's daughter </mark>[<mark>Faustina</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faustina_the_Younger)<mark> in 145.</mark>
<mark>After Antoninus died in 161, Marcus acceded to the throne alongside his adoptive brother, who took the </mark>[<mark>regnal name</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regnal_name)<mark> Lucius Aurelius Verus. Under the </mark>[<mark>reign of Marcus Aurelius</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reign_of_Marcus_Aurelius)<mark>, the Roman Empire witnessed much military conflict. In the East, the Romans fought the </mark>[<mark>Parthian War of Lucius Verus</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parthian_War_of_Lucius_Verus)<mark> with a revitalised </mark>[<mark>Parthian Empire</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parthian_Empire)<mark> and the rebel </mark>[<mark>Kingdom of Armenia</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Armenia_(antiquity))<mark>. Marcus defeated the </mark>[<mark>Marcomanni</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcomanni)<mark>, </mark>[<mark>Quadi</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadi)<mark>, and </mark>[<mark>Iazyges</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iazyges)<mark> in the </mark>[<mark>Marcomannic Wars</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcomannic_Wars)<mark>. These and other </mark>[<mark>Germanic peoples</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples)<mark> began to represent a troubling reality for the Empire. He reduced the silver purity of the </mark>[<mark>Roman currency</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_currency)<mark>, the </mark>[<mark>denarius</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denarius)<mark>. The </mark>[<mark>persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Christians_in_the_Roman_Empire)<mark> appears to have increased during his reign, although his involvement is unlikely since there are no Christian sources ascribing him the blame, and he was praised by </mark>[<mark>Justin Martyr</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Martyr)<mark> and </mark>[<mark>Tertullian</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertullian)<mark>.[3] The </mark>[<mark>Antonine Plague</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonine_Plague)<mark> broke out in 165 or 166 and devastated the </mark>[<mark>population of the Roman Empire</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_of_the_Roman_Empire)<mark>, causing the deaths of five to ten million people. Lucius Verus may have died from the plague in 169. When Marcus himself died in 180, he was succeeded by his son </mark>[<mark>Commodus</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodus)<mark>.</mark>
<mark>Commodus's succession after Marcus has been a subject of debate among both contemporary and modern historians. The </mark>[<mark>column</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Column_of_Marcus_Aurelius)<mark> and </mark>[<mark>equestrian statue</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equestrian_statue_of_Marcus_Aurelius)<mark> of Marcus Aurelius still stand in Rome, where they were erected in celebration of his military victories. As a philosopher, his work </mark>[<mark>*Meditations*</mark>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meditations)<mark> is one of the most important sources for the modern understanding of ancient Stoic philosophy. These writings have been praised by fellow writers, philosophers, monarchs, and politicians centuries after his death.</mark>
